structured.reason: The description contains explicit caveats and minimizing or conditional statements that violate the "entirely positive" criterion. Offending phrases: (1) "though we recommend checking with your dermatologist first" is a warning/caveat about use for psoriasis or eczema sufferers. (2) "Because the loofah wrings out easily, it resists the odor buildup common with traditional loofah pieces" is a minimizing reassurance that admits odor buildup is a problem, and it compares against traditional loofah flaws. (3) "Soak the loofah until it softens, then rinse and wring it out after each use. Hand washing keeps the pads fresh between uses" is conditional care that implies the product only performs well with special handling. (4) "the terry side offers a softer option for sensitive areas" implies the loofah side is not suitable for sensitive areas, a limitation. Under the strict standard, any of these is sufficient to fail.
